title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Despite Nvidia's slide, the Dow jumped over 1,000 points (+2.2%) and the Nasdaq rallied nearly 3% Monday, as markets stayed volatile following Democrats' sweep of Congress.

Markets: Oil fell to its lowest close since August (crude ~$87, -4.2%) as Trump played down imminent new Iran strikes and met with Qatar's PM on mediation efforts; gold rose 1.8% to ~$4,147 and the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.88%.

Companies: Nvidia shares fell 4.3% (down over 5% premarket) after its board launched a probe into CEO Jensen Huang's admitted affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese intelligence operative; investors including Bill Ackman and Gavin Baker are publicly rallying behind Huang amid 'key man risk' and AI-bubble fears.
Companies: Reports say the Trump administration was briefed on the suspected spy operation as early as 2025, opening a new line of Congressional inquiry into Huang's ties to the White House.
Macro/Policy: Today's data - October CPI, ADP employment, the NFIB small-business index, and the NY Fed Q3 household debt report - is the key macro test before the Fed's Dec. 9 meeting.
Macro/Policy: Earnings today include CoreWeave, StubHub, On Holding and Sonos.
